author: Chris Ogden
releaseNotes:
1.5.2 - A safe Reconnect to SignalBricks, also while lock code management is on (#46). Reconnect was hidden while lock code management was on, because its link carries the access token SignalBricks uses for lock control, and the workaround (turn management off, reconnect, turn it back on) dropped the slot rules, fingerprint key, approvals and code changes in progress. Reconnect is now a button that is always shown: a click shows Continue to SignalBricks, a sign-in link that works for 10 minutes. Finishing or cancelling the sign-in replaces the access token and registers the new one, as before. If no sign-in result arrives within 10 minutes, the app replaces the token and registers the new one with the ingestion token it already has, so the link stops working. Only the token changes: lock code management stays on with its slot rules, fingerprint key, approvals, full lock control and pending code changes. New: a registration that fails for a reason that may pass (no answer, timeout, rate limit, SignalBricks unavailable) is retried after about 30 seconds, 2 minutes and 5 minutes, shown in the Connection section; it never goes back to the old token. The "turn lock code management off to reconnect" instructions are gone. No token is logged, and none is shown on the page except inside the open link.
1.5.1 - A clearer page after Connect or Reconnect to SignalBricks (#44), like SignalBricks Integration 1.4.3's. The page SignalBricks sends you back to was unstyled. It is now a centred card that works on a phone and follows the device's light or dark mode, with a coloured marker and a headline for the outcome: Connected, Not connected (sign-in cancelled or denied), Connect link expired, or Connection failed with the reason. Each failure says what to do next. A Back to the app link opens the app's page on the hub by its local IP address, with a note on where to find the app when you are not on the hub's network. The page is still one self-contained response with no external scripts, fonts or images, and it shows no token, authorization code or other part of the callback URL; an OAuth error from SignalBricks is no longer echoed on it, and is shown on the app page as the Last error instead (now escaped there). The connection itself (OAuth, the access token replaced on every callback, registration), telemetry and lock code management are unchanged.
1.5.0 - Lock code management: registered slots and full lock control (signalbricks/platform#684). Nothing changes until SignalBricks sends the new settings, and older app versions ignore them. Registered slots let SignalBricks keep codes with custom names (no SBA:/SBM:): the hub only lets SignalBricks touch such a slot while the lock shows the exact name SignalBricks registered, so a code replaced on the lock is never taken over. A rename keeps the old and new names accepted until the hub sees the new one on the lock. Full lock control, per lock, lets new codes go into empty registered slots outside the admin and managed ranges, and, only on locks you also choose under the new setting Locks SignalBricks may fully control, reach registered codes above the ceiling. Empty slots above the ceiling are never written, and writes outside the admin and managed ranges are refused while a booking code sits at or under the ceiling (the booking apps' minimum code position overlaps SignalBricks' slots). A stricter booking rule guards these paths: names with orb followed by a digit in any case, an upper-case ORB starting a word, or starting with G: or GT:, and codes without a name, are never touched. Registration now lists capabilities relocate, registered_slots and full_control. Telemetry is unchanged.
1.4.1 - Lock code management: a lock driver error on the first command of a set, delete or retry can no longer put the code in a log line or a response (#33). Up to 1.4.0 only relocate caught it; for the others the driver's exception, whose message can carry the code, escaped the endpoint. Now the request gets 502 send_error, nothing is held (a change already held for that slot is left as it was and not reported superseded), the call is given back to its rate limit, and the log records only the exception's class name. On the retry endpoint the retried change is dropped with its code, reported failed (send_error) if it was still in progress. If the send works but reporting the replaced change as superseded fails, the request still succeeds. Telemetry is unchanged.
1.4.0 - Lock code management: new relocate endpoint (#31), POST /locks/:id/codes/:slot/relocate with {name, toSlot?, requestId?}, so SignalBricks can rename a code (for example SBM: to SBA: when its class changes) or move it to another slot without ever having or sending the code. The hub reads the code from the lock itself; it is never in the request, the response, a log line or an event. A move writes the new slot first and deletes the old slot only after re-reading the lock shows the new slot holding the same code, so the code is never left in neither slot; if the new slot doesn't confirm, the old slot is left as it was and the failure is reported. Same rules as set and delete (slot rules, ceiling, SBA:/SBM: names, booking codes always refused, 30 writes a minute, 100 pending changes), plus: the new name must start with SBA: or SBM:, the target must be empty and at or under the ceiling, and a change already in progress on either slot gets 409. The outcome arrives as a relocate_result event (with the new slot's fingerprint when a fingerprint key is held). A move out of an approved adopted slot withdraws that slot's approval. Registration now lists capabilities: ["relocate"]. Telemetry is unchanged.
1.3.5 - New setting "Include door codes (hashed by SignalBricks)", off by default (signalbricks/platform#388). Off, nothing changes: the code used to unlock a lock is removed before sending, as before. On, the code of lock events is sent to SignalBricks over the same authenticated channel; SignalBricks keeps only a keyed hash of it, and only if an admin of your SignalBricks organization has also turned on "Hash door codes from Hubitat telemetry"; otherwise it removes it. Every other secret field (pin, passcode, usedCode, lockCodes) is still removed, other events never carry codes, the app still never reads lockCodes for telemetry, and codes are never logged. A failed event send is now logged by error class only. To use it: update, open the app, turn the setting on, click Done.
1.3.4 - Lock code management: the booking-code guard now matches an upper-case ORB followed by a digit anywhere in a code name (signalbricks/platform#581), the same rule SignalBricks Integration uses to claim its codes. Prefixed booking codes written without a space, such as GT:ORB123-Guest or G:ORB1-Guest, were not recognised before and are now always refused for write, delete and reveal and left out of fingerprints and survey results. Names like ORBIT, Orbit or Corbin are not booking codes. Names SignalBricks writes follow the same rule. Also: the app page and log lines now show the app name with the version (e.g. "SignalBricks Telemetry 1.3.4"), so it can't be mistaken for the separately versioned SignalBricks Integration app; registration and events still send the bare version. Telemetry is unchanged.
1.3.3 - Lock code management: new batch fingerprints endpoint, GET /fingerprints, which returns code fingerprints for every lock selected for code management (or only the locks listed in ?ids=) in one call, so the SignalBricks onboarding wizard and code grouping no longer hit the per-lock limit on hubs with more than 10 locks. It applies exactly the same rules as the per-lock endpoint (never booking codes, never codes). A lock whose codes can't be read is reported on its own without failing the call. Limited to 4 calls a minute, separate from the per-lock limit of 10. Telemetry is unchanged.
1.3.2 - Daily check-in: once a day, at a time picked at random for each hub (never between 2 and 4am hub time), the app checks whether it was updated and, if so, re-registers with SignalBricks, so hubs that send few events still report a new version within a day. It sends nothing when the version is unchanged, and uses the same conditions and 30-minute backoff as 1.3.1. The check-in is set up on Done or Connect, or on the first event after updating from 1.3.1, and removed on Disconnect. The README has a new Updating section on Hubitat Package Manager auto-updates. Telemetry is unchanged.
1.3.1 - After an update through Hubitat Package Manager, the app now re-registers with SignalBricks by itself on the next event (or code-change check), so SignalBricks sees the new version and the onboarding wizard no longer reports the old one. Only when the hub is connected and lock code management is on or was registered, at most every 30 minutes until it succeeds. Events and registration now also report the hub firmware version. Telemetry is unchanged.
1.3.0 - Lock code management: new fingerprints endpoint for the SignalBricks onboarding wizard. SignalBricks can send a per-organization fingerprint key with its slot rules; the hub then returns, for each occupied slot SignalBricks may manage (never booking codes), a short keyed hash (HMAC-SHA256, 16 hex characters) of its code, so SignalBricks can see which slots share a code across locks and hubs without reading any code. The key is never returned or logged, and is dropped when lock code management is turned off or on Disconnect. Limited to 10 calls a minute. SignalBricks can also list a lock as survey-only, so it can read its slots and fingerprints before onboarding without being allowed to change any code on it. Telemetry is unchanged.
1.2.1 - Fixes a registration 403 on hubs connected before lock code management existed. The app now registers with SignalBricks only while lock code management is on, or to turn off a registration it made earlier, so hubs that don't use it no longer register on every Done. If SignalBricks says this hub's token can't enable lock code management, the app shows "Reconnect to SignalBricks to enable lock management" instead of an HTTP 403, and doesn't retry. To enable it on such a hub: reconnect to SignalBricks, then turn lock code management on. Telemetry is unchanged.
1.2.0 - Lock code management: every code set and delete is now verified on the hub. About 30 seconds after the command the app re-reads that slot from the lock (and again up to 3 minutes later), re-sends the command up to 3 times in total if the lock dropped it, and stops early if the slot is no longer allowed or someone else's code is now in it. Each outcome (confirmed, failed or superseded) is reported to SignalBricks as a lock_code_result event without the code. Set and delete accept an optional requestId and return it; a new retry endpoint lets SignalBricks re-send a failed change without re-entering the code. Set and delete are limited to 30 a minute and 100 changes held at once. While a set is being verified, or for up to 24 hours if it fails, the app keeps that code in its own state only (never logged or sent; visible to hub admins on App Status, like the lock's own codes). Telemetry is unchanged.
1.1.1 - Lock code management: the booking-code guard now matches only an upper-case ORB at the start of a name or after a space or hyphen (e.g. ORB123-Guest, GT: ORB123-Guest, Guest-ORB123, Guest -ORB123), so names like Forbes or Orbit are no longer refused. Locks not listed in the SignalBricks slot rules now allow nothing (no fallback to the default ranges). Names SignalBricks writes follow the same rule and also may not contain ORB followed by a digit anywhere (which signalbricksIntegration would claim).
1.1.0 - Optional Lock code management (off by default): separately selected locks get access-token gated endpoints for SignalBricks to list slots (never codes), set/delete admin (SBA:) and managed (SBM:) codes and reveal one code at a time (10/min). The hub only allows the admin and managed ranges SignalBricks configures up to a ceiling set in the app (default 25), plus adopted slots (above the ceiling only with operator approval in the app); slots holding ORB booking codes are always refused. The app registers its cloud endpoint with SignalBricks after Connect. Telemetry is unchanged and still never sends codes. Already-connected hubs: update, enable Lock code management, select locks, click Done.
1.0.0 - Initial release. Read-only lock, contact, temperature, humidity and battery telemetry to SignalBricks with an OAuth (PKCE) Connect flow. The hub access token used during Connect is rotated immediately after the callback. Door codes (PINs) are stripped from event data before sending; only the code slot/name used is sent.
